newsitem.title: USA: Permanent U.S. trade status urged for China.
newsitem.headline: Permanent U.S. trade status urged for China.

text.p: Senate Democratic Leader Tom Daschle said the United States should grant permanent Most Favoured Nation trade status to China instead of renewing it annually.

The MFN issue was expected to go before Congress again in the late spring. In the past critics of the Beijing government have sought to block it or attach conditions on human rights, trade and other issues.

Daschle said on Monday the annual renewal of China's MFN -- which grants China's exports the same tariff treatment accorded to America's other trading partners -- was a disadvantage to the United States and caused uncertainty to business.
Daschle was speaking at a news conference with other members of a Senate delegation just back from a trip to China, Vietnam, Hong Kong and Taiwan.

Several members of the delegation emphasised that China was making progress on human rights, but voiced concern over trade issues they said should be settled before China was admitted to the new World Trade Organisation.
"My personal view is that it is time to extend MFN permanently," Daschle said.

Daschle, who is from the grain exporting state of South Dakota, was in sharp contrast to his predecessor as Democratic leader, former Sen. George Mitchell of Maine, who was a stern critic of the Beijing government.
Daschle said pressure on the human rights issue should continue, "but I don't believe to threaten in some way to curtail or eliminate that (trade) relationship is in our best interest."
